title: Tool‑Augmented Post‑Processing of Identical LLM Candidates for Intent‑Driven Network Configuration (shared_initial_candidate evaluation)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (cand_netops_toolagent_003_v1) that isolates whether deterministic post‑processing (a topology‑aware deterministic verifier + lightweight simulator) changes a deterministic validator pass/fail outcome when the exact same single LLM candidate is supplied verbatim to both pipelines (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Design: 300 paired tasks (one shared generation per task), paired binary estimator on deterministic‑validator pass. Completed: 598 episodes → 299 analyzable pairs. Result (artifact‑grounded): contingency n11=299, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0; paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10k resamples, seed=1729). One planned pair was excluded after a provider failure; failure traces and the execution log are archived. Conclusion: under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and this synthetic task pool, deterministic post‑processing confirmed rather than changed the binary verdict for identical candidates. We archive all raw responses, provider traces, validator traces, scoring JSONs, and the full SHA‑256 manifest to permit audit and replication; limitations and recommended follow‑ups (independent per‑condition generation, adversarial strata, multi‑model replication) are discussed.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are widely proposed for NetOps tasks such as intent→configuration translation, repair, and automatable maintenance. A widespread architectural pattern pairs an LLM generator with deterministic post‑processing (validators, simulators, or formal checkers) to increase operational trustworthiness. Empirically attributing downstream improvements either to (A) changed generation or (B) deterministic post‑processing requires an experimental design that isolates those components. We therefore preregistered a narrowly scoped confirmatory study whose sole intervention was deterministic post‑processing applied to identical LLM candidates (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Research question: Does deterministic verifier+simulator post‑processing change a deterministic‑validator pass/fail verdict when both pipelines receive the identical LLM candidate? Contributions: (1) a fully preregistered, fully archived paired experiment (cand_netops_toolagent_003_v1) with per‑file SHA‑256 evidence for all key artifacts; (2) an exact, artifact‑traceable confirmatory numeric result (n11=299, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0; p=1.0; bootstrap CI=[0.00,0.00]); (3) a focused discussion of ceiling effects, operational implications, and prescriptive guidance for designs that can test tool‑augmented generation.
sections.related_work: We position this study relative to recent verified work on intent‑driven configuration and verifier‑assisted generation. Representative, verified sources that informed the design include intent→configuration methods and system‑level tool‑augmentation surveys (e.g., Nguyen et al., 2024; PreConfig arXiv:2403.09369), and engineering reports on tool‑augmented agents; these works motivated paired designs, verifier requirement lists, and the need for artifact hashing and preregistration. Our experiment is not a synthesis or improvement over those systems; instead it isolates a single procedural question (shared‑candidate post‑processing) that appears in the pipeline design space of many prior publications. Exact cited artifacts used for positioning are listed in the Cited Record Ids field and are archived in the evidence bundle.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The study preregistration cand_netops_toolagent_003_v1 froze: (a) primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline on a deterministic‑validator pass indicator; (b) shared_initial_candidate semantics (one LLM call per task reused verbatim by both pipelines); (c) planned n=300 paired tasks stratified by difficulty (150 simple, 150 complex); (d) analysis executor = paired_binary_analysis_v1; (e) missingness and exclusion rules (complete‑pair handling; exact matches to public corpora moved to exploratory). Preregistration SHA‑256: 991674d51794b41cf66471509149237b9a99f709b69aa3408d3d9d2ea2d50fc0 (archived). Experimental pipeline (artifact‑grounded). - Generator: declared model gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json; SHA‑256: 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. - Shared_initial semantics: for each task the system made one LLM generation that was stored and reused verbatim by both the baseline and guarded pipelines (proof artifacts: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 8f38c8be..., execution/provider_calls/task-000001-shared-initial.json SHA‑256 fd046204...). - Deterministic validator/simulator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (version 5.0) parses CLI candidates, enforces workflow invariants (e.g., make_before_break, shutdown_configure_restore), computes final_state snapshots and violation codes, and returns a binary pass/fail indicator plus normalized_configuration and difficulty metadata. Every scoring JSON contains validator_trace with final_state and violation list (examples: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA‑256 6569b491... and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 cefa6344...). Tasks and sampling. Tasks were synthesized from a deterministic synthetic topology pool with explicit initial_state, expected_final_state, intent text, required_sequence, and difficulty metadata; these manifests and their hashes are archived (execution/task_manifest.jsonl and execution/execution_manifest.json). Planned maximum provider calls = 600 (one shared generation per task, two scoring evaluations). Stopping rules and failures. The preregistration defines complete‑pair inclusion and logs all technical failures. One planned pair (pair‑000269) was excluded because the shared_initial generation provider call failed; the provider failure and the execution log entry are archived (execution/provider_calls/task-000269-shared-initial.json and execution/execution_log.jsonl; see execution manifest for hashes). Analysis plan. Primary analysis used the frozen paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor: exact McNemar two‑sided test and paired bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). All analysis inputs/outputs are archived under analysis/ and hashed.
sections.results: Execution footprint and sample. Planned: 600 episodes (300 pairs). Completed: 598 episodes; failed: 2; analyzable complete pairs: 299 (execution/execution_manifest.json records these counts). Model calls used = 300 (one shared generation per task). Primary confirmatory result (artifact‑grounded): analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 d77df43abf...) records n11=299, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0. Baseline success rate = 299/299 = 100.0%; guarded success rate = 299/299 = 100.0%. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.00, 0.00] (artifact: analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg SHA‑256 ae5b8e0c...). Representative episode artifacts (examples, all archived): - Task pair‑000001 shared candidate: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 8f38c8be...); scoring traces: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 6569b491...), execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 cefa6344...). - Task pair‑000002 shared candidate and scoring traces: execution/responses/task-000002-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 ae967f70...), execution/scoring/task-000002-baseline.json (SHA‑256 77f6d653...), execution/scoring/task-000002-guarded.json (SHA‑256 696640e6...). Missingness and failures. One pair (pair‑000269) was excluded per the preregistered complete‑pair rule because the shared_initial generation provider call failed; the provider error is logged and archived in execution/execution_log.jsonl and in the provider call trace execution/provider_calls/task-000269-shared-initial.json (see execution manifest for file paths and SHA‑256s). No scorable discordant pairs were observed in the confirmatory set (zero n10, n01). Secondary estimands. Because discordant pairs are zero, secondary exploratory estimands (simulated outage incidence, cost trade‑offs) are not informative in this shared‑candidate execution; raw latency and provider call counts remain archived for exploratory inspection (execution/provider_calls/* and execution/responses/*).
sections.discussion: Interpretation. For the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and the synthetic task pool used here, deterministic post‑processing (validator + simulator) confirmed the LLM candidate rather than changing the binary deterministic‑validator verdict: every analyzable pair produced acceptance by both pipelines (n11=299). This is an exact, artifact‑traceable observation — the numerical contingency and per‑task scoring JSONs are archived with SHA‑256s. Ceiling effect and statistical power. The preregistration assumed a lower baseline pass rate (~0.60) and aimed to detect an absolute paired improvement of 0.20; the observed baseline = 1.00 created a ceiling effect that renders the preregistered minimally important effect unobservable in this run. The degenerate bootstrap CI ([0.00,0.00]) reflects zero within‑pair variance. Operational implications. - When LLM generation quality is high in the evaluated task distribution, the role of deterministic validators may be primarily auditative: producing normalized configurations, explicit violation codes, final_state snapshots, and machine‑readable justification traces rather than changing binary outcomes for identical candidates. - Validators remain essential for auditability and failure explanation (each scoring JSON includes validator_trace with final_state and violation list). - To evaluate whether tool‑augmented agents improve generation outcomes, experimental designs must allow independent per‑condition generation (no shared candidates), include adversarial/higher‑difficulty strata to avoid ceiling saturation, and replicate across models. Reproducibility and auditability. All claims above are reproducible from archived artifacts: execution/execution_manifest.json (full per‑file SHA‑256 manifest), execution/responses/*.txt (shared_initial candidates and per‑condition outputs), execution/provider_calls/*.json (provider traces), execution/scoring/*.json (validator traces), and analysis/* (paired contingency and analysis outputs). Representative artifact pointers (with SHA‑256s) are: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 8f38c8be...), execution/provider_calls/task-000001-shared-initial.json (SHA‑256 fd046204...), execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 6569b491...), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 d77df43abf...). Limitations (artifact‑grounded). See the Limitations section below for a concise enumerated list. Recommendations for follow‑ups. (1) Independent per‑condition generation to measure generation effects (no shared candidate). (2) Include adversarial/harder task strata to avoid ceiling effects. (3) Multi‑model replication across LLM families and seed variation. (4) Instrumented repair‑loop ablations to measure the contribution of repair iterations (preregistered exploratory questions E1–E3).
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a tightly scoped paired experiment that isolated deterministic post‑processing for identical LLM candidates. For the 299 analyzable pairs the deterministic validator accepted the identical candidate in every pair (n11=299, no discordant pairs). The observed paired difference is 0.00 (McNemar p = 1.0; bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.00]). This result is artifact‑grounded and reproducible from the archived manifest. It demonstrates that, in this setting, post‑processing served to confirm rather than to change the verifier verdict. To evaluate whether tool‑augmented agents improve generation outcomes, future confirmatory runs must vary generation between conditions, include adversarial tasks, and replicate across models and seeds. All raw artifacts, provider traces, validator traces, scoring JSONs, and the per‑file SHA‑256 manifest are archived for audit and replication (execution/execution_manifest.json and associated file hashes).

limitations: This run used shared_initial_candidate semantics and therefore isolates only deterministic post‑processing for identical candidates; it cannot measure whether tool‑augmented generation (i.e., allowing the agent to call verifiers or simulators during generation or to produce repaired candidates) improves generation correctness or reduces outages.
Tasks were synthetic and executed in a lightweight topology simulator; external validity to vendor‑specific CLIs, firmware idiosyncrasies, or production telemetry is limited.
Only one declared model family (gpt‑5‑mini) was used; results do not generalize across model families without replication.

The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) encodes curated workflow invariants and provides operationally meaningful checks, but it cannot exhaustively represent all production device behaviors or operator policies.
Observed baseline success = 100% produced a ceiling effect; the preregistered minimally important effect (0.20) was therefore unobservable in this run.
